__comment: Item definitions: every good a dwarf can carry or store, from mined stone and food to tools,
packed furniture and coins. Ids are base:item:<name>, with no kind in them: what an item belongs
to is said by its material_tags (doc 13, 'Naming ids and files').
Loaded by ContentRegistry (doc 13); ItemDropManager keeps its own copy.
Fields:
display_name  — human-readable name shown in UI and tooltips
plural_name   — the name for several, where it is not display_name plus s (Events lines)
description   — one-sentence flavour text shown in the inspect panel
model         — path to the 1:16 voxel .glb model (res:// path)
crate_capacity — opted-in crate packaging capacity (24: produce, seeds, cuttings and
log torches); absent means one unit
crate_models  — low / half / full models for counts 1-8 / 9-16 / 17-24
One crate occupies one ground cell or furniture slot. Loose drops
use the same crate; packaging is automatic and costs no resources.
carry_cost    — positive points per physical item against hauling.carry_capacity
A crate pays once regardless of fill; missing costs default to 1.
weight_class  — 'light' | 'heavy' — affects dwarf haul speed
light: full haul speed; heavy: ×0.7 haul speed while any heavy item
is in the load; independent of carry_cost
material_tags — flat string array; must include at least one 'stockpile_*' tag
used by stockpile zone filters and crafting ingredient queries
food          — edible goods: edible, nutrition (hunger filled by one portion),
keeps_days (days a stack lasts at 20°C under a roof before it rots;
doc 42 'Spoilage', the rest in task_config.json food.spoilage) and
serving (the meal's presentation shape and colour)
__comment_stone: Raw stone blocks — heavy, common, used for construction

base:item:rough_stone.description: A rough-hewn chunk of mountain stone. Dwarves use it to wall up and backfill unwanted openings.

__comment_starter_tools: Tool goods (doc 306). Workers make the Ranger's kit and the stone hammer at the crude workbench; Blacksmiths hammer the copper pick, saw, chisel and hoe on the anvil stone from a copper bar and a log (doc 310; at the basic smelter until 2026-11-14). A dwarf promoted to a tool career collects and equips its tool; equipment: tier, materials and benefit word the Equipment view; dig_time is the share of the digging time its holder needs (the copper pick's 0.8, read by DwarfAssets.mining_duration_multiplier).

equipment.benefit: Enables the Ranger profession. They fish with its rod; the spear waits for hunting. No work-speed bonus. The kit stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:ranger_kit.description: A stone-tipped spear and a peeled fishing rod, crossed and lashed together. Collected and equipped when promoting a Ranger; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

equipment.benefit: Enables the Blacksmith profession. They hammer copper bars into the other trades' tools with it. No work-speed bonus. The hammer stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:stone_hammer.description: A stone head and wooden handle. Collected and equipped when promoting a Blacksmith; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

equipment.benefit: Enables the Miner profession. Digging takes 20% less time than with a Worker's stone pick, and the Miner's levels take off more. The pick stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:copper_pick.description: A copper head on a wooden haft, hammered from a bar on the anvil stone. Collected and equipped when promoting a Miner; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

equipment.benefit: Enables the Carpenter profession. No work-speed bonus. The saw stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:copper_saw.description: A pull saw: a thin copper blade set in a long straight handle bound with cord, cutting as it is drawn back. Collected and equipped when promoting a Carpenter; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

equipment.benefit: Enables the Stonemason profession. They drive it with the maul. No work-speed bonus. The chisel stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:copper_chisel.description: A copper chisel and the hammerstone maul that drives it, lashed together. Collected and equipped when promoting a Stonemason; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

equipment.benefit: Enables the Farmer profession: hoeing, sowing and harvesting the colony's fields. No work-speed bonus. The hoe stays equipped until this dwarf changes profession.

base:item:copper_hoe.description: A copper blade on a wooden haft, hammered from a bar on the anvil stone. Collected and equipped when promoting a Farmer; returned to colony supplies when changing professions.

__comment_soil: Soft earth — one Soil good, dug from grass, dirt and cave soil

base:item:soil.description: Loose earth dug from grass, dirt and cave soil.

__comment_ore: Metal ore chunks — heavy, moderate trade value

base:item:copper_ore.description: A green-tinged ore chunk, the first metal dwarves learn to smelt.

base:item:tin_ore.description: A soft grey ore found near the surface. Easy to smelt, useful for early tools.

base:item:iron_ore.description: A heavy reddish ore, the backbone of dwarven industry.

base:item:silver_ore.description: A pale lustrous ore found in mid-depth veins. Valuable for fine metalwork and trade.

base:item:coal.description: A brittle black rock that burns long and hot.

base:item:gold_ore.description: A gleaming heavy ore. Even raw it catches every torch.

__comment_metal: Smelted metal (doc 297): copper bars from the basic smelter, stored as Metal (stockpile_metal). Copper fittings were removed on 2026-11-13 (doc 306): what would have taken fittings takes bars.

base:item:copper_bar.description: A rough bar of copper cast in a stone mould at the basic smelter. Blacksmiths hammer it into the trades' tools, and learn their own trade on it before iron.

__comment_gem: Finished gem drops — naturally brilliant, ready to trade; no jeweller or cutting step. Stable _raw keys are identifiers only.

base:item:jade_raw.description: A lustrous mint-green gem with broad, gleaming facets. Beautiful straight from the rock and ready to trade.

base:item:amethyst_raw.description: A brilliant violet gem whose pale facets catch the torchlight. Ready to treasure or trade as soon as it is mined.

base:item:ruby_raw.description: A rich crimson gem with bright, glassy facets, freed from deep volcanic stone. Needs no further finishing.

base:item:sapphire_raw.description: A royal-blue gem with icy flashes across its facets. Already brilliant when it leaves the rock.

base:item:emerald_raw.description: A vivid green gem from the deepest rock seams, with crisp mint-bright facets. Ready to trade without further work.

base:item:diamond_raw.description: A dazzling gem with ice-blue and warm white facets, beautiful straight from the uttermost dark. Merchants go silent when they see one.

base:item:fossil_fragment.description: A stone impression of an ancient creature. Scholars pay handsomely.

base:item:pine_log.description: A straight-grained softwood log, light and easy to work. The backbone of early construction.

base:item:oak_log.description: A dense hardwood log with a tight grain. Prized for furniture and barrel staves.

base:item:oak_stave.description: A split plank of seasoned oak shaped for cooperage. Essential for crafting aging casks.

base:item:apple_log.description: A fine-grained pinkish wood. Burns slowly with a sweet scent, useful for smoking and light carpentry.

base:item:juniper_log.description: A fragrant hardwood log with dense, knotted grain.

__comment_planks: Sawn timber (doc 308; owner, 2026-11-13: a Carpenter starts with a saw, so its goods need not be rudimentary). A Carpenter saws one log into two planks of its wood at the carpenter's bench, and the Carpenter's plank furniture is made from them. Stored as Planks (stockpile_plank), on the ground and on the finished goods pallet, four to a quarter. Each log carries a tag of its own name (pine_log, apple_log) so that its sawing recipe takes that log alone. Never timber: a nightly fire burns logs, not planks.

base:item:pine_plank.description: A thick board sawn from a pine log with the Carpenter's copper saw. Pale and light, the plainest of the planks.

base:item:oak_plank.description: A thick board sawn from an oak log with the Carpenter's copper saw. Dense and tight-grained, for furniture meant to last.

base:item:juniper_plank.description: A thick board sawn from a juniper log with the Carpenter's copper saw. Fragrant and knotted, with a warm dark heart.

base:item:apple_plank.description: A thick board sawn from an applewood log with the Carpenter's copper saw. Fine-grained and pinkish, the handsomest of the planks.

__comment_flora: Harvested plant matter — crops, berries, seeds

base:item:elderberry.description: Dark purple clusters with a tart depth. The classic base for mountain wine.

base:item:blueberry.description: Sweet high-altitude berries with a clean finish. Prized for mead and summer ales.

base:item:wild_strawberry.description: Tiny and intensely sweet. Merchants go quiet when they see a basket of these.

base:item:juniper_berry.description: Tart blue-black berries with a resinous bite. Prized for gin-style brewing.

base:item:plump_helmet.description: A bulbous purple mushroom that grows fast in moist cave soil.

base:item:pig_tail.description: A curling fibrous plant that can be spun into rough cloth.

base:item:apple.description: A crisp mountain apple. Sweet enough to eat raw, better pressed into cider.

__comment_vegetables: Vegetables (doc 309): what a Farmer pulls from a field's tilled soil, tile_yield of them a tile (data/flora/field_crops.json). Eaten raw, a portion each, as fruit is.

base:item:radish.description: A crisp red radish, the first thing out of the ground in spring. It does not keep long.

base:item:carrot.description: A sweet orange carrot pulled in summer. Good raw, and it keeps a while in a cool store.

base:item:turnip.description: A white turnip with purple shoulders. It keeps like apples, so it is the root a colony stores for winter.

base:item:cabbage.description: A heavy pale green head. A lot of food from one plant, but it wilts within days.

base:item:onion.description: A golden onion with a papery skin. Dried in its skin, it keeps longer than any other field food.

base:item:pumpkin.description: A great orange pumpkin, cut into portions. It keeps for a season in a cool store.

base:item:kale.description: Dark, frilled winter leaves, picked from the standing plant through the snow.

__comment_fish: Fish — caught from Fishing zones, one kind for each water (doc 289). Eaten raw, or grilled at a burning campfire (doc 290).

base:item:perch.description: A barred lake perch with orange fins. Good eating, but it keeps only a couple of days unless it is kept cool.

base:item:trout.description: A river trout, olive-brown with dark and red spots and a silver belly. Good eating, but it keeps only a couple of days unless it is kept cool.

base:item:char.description: A mountain tarn's char: a green back with pale spots and a red-orange belly. Good eating, and it keeps a day longer than other fresh fish, longer still if it is kept cool.

base:item:cave_fish.description: A pale, eyeless fish from the spring cave's pool. Good eating, but it keeps only a couple of days unless it is kept cool.

base:item:dried_fish.description: Fish split and dried on a rack. Tough, salty and filling, and it keeps about thirty days, longer kept cool.

__comment_seed: Seeds — planted by dwarves to start new crop growth

base:item:pine_cone.description: A seed-bearing cone from a mature pine. Plant it and wait a few seasons.

base:item:oak_acorn.description: A small but promising acorn. Oaks are slow to grow and worth every year of the wait.

base:item:apple_seed.description: A seed pressed from a mountain apple. Give it good soil and a few seasons.

base:item:elderberry_cutting.description: A fresh stem cutting from an elderberry bush. Root it in surface soil to grow a new bush.

base:item:blueberry_cutting.description: A small blueberry stem. Plant it on rocky high-ground soil for best results.

base:item:wild_strawberry_cutting.description: A runner cutting from a wild strawberry plant. Grows quickly in good surface soil.

base:item:pig_tail_seed.description: A small hard seed from a pig tail plant. Sow in surface dirt before summer for a full season's fiber harvest.

base:item:juniper_seed.description: A hard dark seed that takes root slowly but grows into a towering tree.

__comment_drink: Finished brewed drinks — colony morale and trade goods

base:item:ale.description: A dark, malty ale brewed from cave wheat or plump helmets.

base:item:mead.description: A golden honey-wine brewed from sweet pods. Light, complex, and expensive.

__comment_misc2: Processed goods — outputs from non-brewing workshops

base:item:cloth.description: A coarse woven fabric spun from pig tail fibers.

base:item:water_bucket.description: A wooden bucket filled from a well or underground stream.

__comment_new_flora: New brewing crops — hops and grapes

base:item:hops.description: Papery green cones with a sharp, resinous bite. The bitter backbone of any proper ale.

base:item:grape.description: Heavy purple clusters from the mountain vine terraces. Sweet, complex, and worth the wait.

__comment_honey: Honey — produced by beehives, used in mead and cider

base:item:honey.description: Thick golden honey from mountain beehives. Adds body and sweetness to brewed drinks.

__comment_new_seeds: New plant propagation items — hops and grape cuttings

base:item:hops_cutting.description: A rooted stem cutting from a mature hops bine. Plant it on surface soil before summer.

base:item:grape_cutting.description: A short cane cutting from a fruiting grape vine. Takes a season to establish but lasts for years.

__comment_new_drinks: New brewed drinks — stout, cider, wine, gin, and their aged variants

base:item:stout.description: A thick, near-black ale with a roasted bitterness. Dwarves call it 'proper drinking'.

base:item:cider.description: A crisp, lightly honeyed apple cider. Brisk and refreshing after a long shift in the mines.

base:item:wine.description: A deep, tannic wine pressed from mountain grapes. Not a dwarf's first choice, but the merchants love it.

base:item:gin.description: A sharp, resinous spirit distilled from juniper berries. An acquired taste — and a profitable one.

__comment_aged_drinks: Aged premium variants — produced in the aging cellar, high trade value

base:item:aged_stout.description: A stout that has sat in oak for a month of cold stone silence. Smooth, complex, and deeply satisfying.

base:item:vintage_wine.description: An oak-aged mountain wine that has mellowed into something extraordinary. Caravans will pay dearly.

base:item:reserve_gin.description: Juniper gin rested in oak until the harsh edge softens to something almost elegant.

__comment_special: Special items — unique or limited-use objects that anchor major game flows

base:item:settlement_flag.description: The colony's settlement marker, packed for storage or relocation. Place it to mark the settlement's new location.

__comment_furniture: Furniture items - the carryable forms of placeable furniture. Fetched by FETCH_BUILD leases and restocked on uninstall. All packed furniture shares packed_furniture.glb, an 8x8x8-voxel wooden shipping crate (one world block); the ghost says which piece it becomes. The log torch alone is kept as fruit is, 24 to a crate of its own (crate_capacity, owner 2026-11-15): a plan takes one torch out of a crate, and its sticks show their wood (material_palette).

base:item:bench.description: Two boards pegged onto two plank ends, with a stretcher between them. Packed in a wooden crate.

base:item:hearth.description: Fieldstones and logs packed for a compact stone room heater with an open firebox.

base:item:door_2.description: Rough logs and wooden pegs packed for a 2-block-wide doorway.

base:item:crude_workbench.description: A rough crafting stump packed for installation. Workers can use it from any open side.

base:item:torch.description: A charred branch bound with rough fibre, to hang on a wooden wall peg. A basic light for the first tunnels. Torches are kept 24 to a crate.

__comment_currency: Currency — gold coins earned through trade with merchants and travelers

base:item:gold_coin.description: A minted coin accepted by every merchant on the mountain road. Spend it or hoard it.

base:item:blueberry_bush.description: A living mature shrub with its roots wrapped. Replant through Place › Plants. Preserves its crop state.

base:item:elderberry_bush.description: A living mature shrub with its roots wrapped. Replant through Place › Plants. Preserves its crop state.

base:item:wild_strawberry_bush.description: A living mature shrub with its roots wrapped. Replant through Place › Plants. Preserves its crop state.

base:item:flowers_1.description: A living flower clump with wrapped roots. Replant through Place › Plants. Keeps its shape and seasonal bloom.

base:item:flowers_2.description: A living flower clump with wrapped roots. Replant through Place › Plants. Keeps its shape and seasonal bloom.

base:item:flowers_3.description: A living flower clump with wrapped roots. Replant through Place › Plants. Keeps its shape and seasonal bloom.

base:item:crude_ladder.description: A bundle of split rails and pegged rungs. Installs four blocks of wooden ladder.

base:item:campfire.description: Unlit logs and rough stones packed for a campfire.

base:item:log_stool.description: One small stump stool packed for installation.

base:item:wet_stone.description: Supplies water while deliberately placed. Inactive when packed, carried or stored.

base:item:dry_stone.description: Absorbs excess water above its retained level while placed. Inactive when packed, carried or stored.

base:item:door_3.description: Rough logs and wooden pegs packed for a 3-block-wide doorway.

base:item:door_4.description: Rough logs and wooden pegs packed for a 4-block-wide doorway.

base:item:log_bed.description: Rough bed logs, loose hay and dried leaves packed in a carrying crate.

base:item:log_fence.description: Stands in the middle of a tile. Two level rails join posts on neighboring tiles, forming straight runs, corners and junctions.

base:item:log_gate.description: Hangs across one tile between posts on the tiles either side, sharing posts with connected fences. Opens as dwarves approach and does not seal a room.

base:item:board_game_table.description: A game scratched across the top of a plank table, with loose stones for counters. Add one stool for solo play, or two opposite stools to play together for more happiness.

base:item:drying_rack.description: Two forked posts and a crossbar lashed with rope, for drying fish into food that keeps a season.

base:item:carpenter_bench.description: A hewn slab and four peeled log legs with their rails, packed for installation: the Carpenter's own workbench.

base:item:mason_bench.description: A split stone slab and two log stumps, packed for installation: the Stonemason's own workbench.

base:item:basic_smelter.description: The great stone and the casting stone of a basic smelter, packed for installation: the Blacksmith's own workbench.

base:item:anvil_stone.description: One great stone with its top split off level, packed for installation: the Blacksmith's anvil.

base:item:tool_rack.description: A sawn board and its pegs, packed for installation against a wall.

base:item:raw_materials_crate.description: The posts and boards of a raw materials crate, packed for installation on the floor.

base:item:finished_goods_pallet.description: The deck boards and runners of a finished goods pallet, packed for installation on the floor.

base:item:food_shelf.description: The plank ends and shelves of a food shelf, packed for installation on the floor.

base:item:stone_stool.description: One stone stool, a rough stone knocked square, packed for installation.

base:item:dining_table.description: Four broad boards pegged across two plank ends. Place the table and add stools separately.
